name: Fused lantern-staff
slug: Fused lantern and staff that reveals the Ethereal Plane and draws nearby spirits when the active staff is held.
description: One fused item: the Staff of the Lantern Bearer, a name the DM confirms and that Sylan also remembers as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper, joined to a hooded, finely made Lantern of Revealing with an aura of evocation and two settings. The pieces are listed among the magic items from the white dragon hoard, dated November 3 of the previous year; Play traces the lantern to Ord in Volga and the staff to Sylan at Shades and Trades, and the DM says the lantern was identified at Shades and Trades. They were already drawn together, as if polarized or magnetized, and fused in a short earlier working when the lantern's inscription was read. The DM confirms they are fused. One setting blinded everyone in the room, and command words produced an effect the party failed to cleanly undo. On November 3, campaign year 25, Ord's experiment showed him the Ethereal Plane and blinded him until lesser restoration; no spirits were present then. The inscription is not in the DM's current notes. Ord offers "Brightest day in darkness" as the ignition phrase, and the DM treats the real wording as still to be settled.

log.summary: Used throughout the lantern trial in the woods, by the same steps as before, so bystanders would not be blinded. Ord and Sylan close their eyes. When lit, the lantern glows a desaturated blue and shows the Ethereal Plane as grayscale, semi-opaque, and ghostly, including otherwise unnoticed shadows; it is unconfirmed whether that sight penetrates magical darkness. Ethereal beings can take hold of the crook, and contact makes them burn away from the edges like paper while they howl inside the hearer's head. When Sylan grabs the active staff—while it is active he describes it as having no lantern—the lantern becomes incandescent shadow, a glowing roiling ball of shadow, and spirits within about four feet are vacuumed into him as a byproduct; he feels nothing. Joined hands throw a black luminescent beacon into the sky, and letting go ends it: the clearing dies in light, a faint outline remains for a few blinks, and Ord's wireframe spirit-sight continues until he turns that off separately. Sylan treats the fusion as having been part of the plan, still asks whether the inscriptions can be tried separately, and does not have the lantern on his sheet. A misremembered lantern name was "lantern of the staff keeper." Ord proposes saying the incantation backwards to shut it off; the last time they tried to turn this kind of effect off, something else happened, and the backward attempt is not resolved. Sylan says they should never touch it again because it always brings those terrible things.
notes: One fused item, used throughout the lantern trial. The staff half is the Staff of the Lantern Bearer. Sylan also remembers that name as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper, and the DM confirms the staff name. The lantern half is a Lantern of Revealing. A misremembered lantern name was 'lantern of the staff keeper.' Sylan, while it is active, describes the staff as having no lantern.

log.summary: Sylan and Ord confirm the lantern and staff have fused. Gerk calls it a hoard-bought staff of lantern-something. An exact activation word is never spoken. The incantation blinds anyone who looks: Sylan avoids it by not looking, and Gerk, away from the others, is blinded without knowing whether he looked. During the incantation the wielder sees a grayscale Ethereal Plane; that is how Ord saw the spirits on Sylan. When Sylan takes the staff he sees those spirits, a black pillar rises, and they are drawn into him rather than the staff. His idea that it blinds for Ord and gathers spirits for him is only a working theory. Ord hands it to Sylan to test another wielder. Taking it causes no immediate disaster, but Sylan cannot wield a greatsword while holding it. In Trigash Forest it shows Ord the spirits following Sylan. The party can already see spirits, so those can be moved on. Haldor calls the event the big light, treats the item as summoning undead, illegal in New Navel, and will confiscate it unless hidden. Sylan agrees to hide it and to identify the fused form at Shades and Trades if that was not already done.

log.summary: Also called the staff with the light bringer, the fused lantern-staff is now held by Sylan, to whom Ord gave it. It resembles a shepherd's crook of very hardy wood with a square, medieval-style lantern open on all sides at its end, its frame inscribed in archaic or arcane script. It emanates a palpable magical presence, visible in how light catches it, and Dana confirmed it is magical with a 22 Arcana check. It is activated by a four-line oath, the 'Seeker passphrase', ending 'Lantern keeper's light', with the user closing their eyes on the fourth line. Activation drains color toward the holder, rendering surroundings grayscale and high-contrast, casts a mild chill across the whole stronghold, and overlays a hazy view of another dimension; the holder appears as a silver spectral outline. Doors opened while it is active collapse into blackness, and opening one pulled a nearby soul into Sylan. Focusing its light on an object reveals residual souls and can prompt a response. Switching it off leaves the environment deadened until torches rewarm the area. A previous use caused a vortex in the sky and blinded Gerk, and it previously let Ord see souls attached to objects.
